html:
Charlotte was Grand Duchess of Luxembourg from 1919 to 1964, the ruler who became the symbol of the country's survival in the Second World War.

She came to the throne when her sister was forced to abdicate for siding too closely with the German occupiers of the First World War. A referendum in 1919 kept the monarchy, with Charlotte at its head.

When Germany invaded in May 1940 she fled, and from London she spoke to her people over the BBC. She came home in 1945 as a national figure. Her reign saw Luxembourg drop neutrality, join NATO and help found the European communities. She abdicated in favour of her son Jean in 1964.
